thread:
maria: Alert from monitoring: rtg1 controlplane authz token validation error rate jumped to 42% over the last 2m. Console requests 503, GPU provisioning hitting backoff. metric link: https://grafana.redwood/rtg1/alert/824
aj: seeing same in logs, auth-proxy returning 500s and timeouts. provisioning service is failing to get signed tokens.
sophia: any recent rollout? config push to controlplane yesterday at 03:00 UTC. rollout shows successful but maybe side-effect.
liam: I didn't push anything to auth. There was a batch NAT change in rtg1 network at 04:15; cloud changed ephemeral SNAT range — could be related to token validation upstream. network-bot: BGP flaps and SNAT churn recorded for rtg1 from 04:10-04:25.
maria: console calls authz/token and then hits kv-store. If token validation fails we fall back to provisioning backoff. Can someone confirm token-store latency?
aj: kv-store p99 for token-lookup is 230ms (baseline 30ms). logs: ```auth-proxy ERROR token validation timeout: ctx deadline exceeded```
tina: autoscaler observed many failed allocation attempts and is applying exponential backoff, GPUs in pool-rtg1 show many 'pending' longer than 10m.
sophia: quick mitigation: route controlplane auth traffic to na-east1 fallback cluster (cached keys) until rtg1 stable. That requires a routing rule flip in TrafficManager. Who can enact?
liam: I can flip TrafficManager route, but must coordinate with infra to ensure capacity in na-east1. We may incur extra cost. @maria can you approve?
maria: approve for emergency traffic shift. Prioritize console & provisioning paths. :white_check_mark:
aj: initiating canary reroute step: running command: ```tmctl route set controlplane-auth --from=rtg1 --to=na-east1 --percent=20``` monitoring error rate.
deploy-bot: tmctl change accepted, rollout id tm-2026-1902003333-c1.
network-bot: BGP SNAT churn subsided at 04:28, but we still see elevated packet loss on one transit peer (peer-7).
aj: after 10m canary error rate dropped to 6% on routed traffic. increasing to 60% now.
sophia: while traffic is shifted, plan: 1) scale auth-proxy replicas in rtg1 + increase token cache TTL, 2) restart kv-store replicas sequentially to clear slow nodes, 3) run health check. Who owns step 1?
liam: scaling auth-proxy to x6 in rtg1 now: ```kubectl -n controlplane scale deployment auth-proxy --replicas=6 --context=rtg1```
tina: provisioning backoff thresholds cleared for a subset after scaling, but some GPUs still pending — likely due to earlier allocation failures. I'm manually draining the oldest pending pods to retrigger scheduling.
aj: restarting kv-store pod kv-3 in rtg1: ```kubectl -n controlplane delete pod kv-3 --context=rtg1``` monitoring replication lag.
maria: once we see p99 token lookup back to <50ms and auth error rate <1% we'll start shifting traffic back. ETA 20-30m.
network-bot: cloud provider notes minor internal NAT reconfiguration impacted return path for some SNAT sessions; provider filed ticket CP-5342.
sophia: token cache TTL increased from 30s -> 300s in rollout config; patch pushed to controlplane config.
aj: p99 token lookup at 38ms now, auth error rate 0.7% overall, console 200s recovering.
liam: starting gradual shift back: ```tmctl route set controlplane-auth --from=na-east1 --to=rtg1 --percent=30```
deploy-bot: tmctl change accepted, rollout id tm-2026-1902003333-c2.
maria: provisioning metrics trending to normal, GPUs allocations recovering, no further backoff spikes. Great job folks.
sophia: postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC, owners: network+controlplane. Action items: provider RCA follow-up, add SNAT observability, durable token cache fallback, and runbook update for tmctl reroutes.
liam: closing incident channel when everyone ACKs. :v:
